prompt:
The Harbor mobile app must query crew voyages as **one object** without seeing the join. Ad-hoc SQL from the app should remain a single SELECT (not EXEC). Reporting will filter and join the result to other tables.

Which object should you create?
explanation: Views encapsulate joins and remain composable in FROM/JOIN. Procedures are invoked with EXEC, not composed like tables. A trigger is the wrong side-effect for a read model. Returning XML from a scalar UDF is neither set-based nor what the app asked for.
code:
CREATE OR ALTER VIEW dbo.vCrewVoyages
AS
SELECT c.CrewId, c.Handle, v.VoyageId, v.VoyageDate
FROM dbo.Crew AS c
INNER JOIN dbo.Voyage AS v ON v.CrewId = c.CrewId;

options.text: A view — callers SELECT from it like a table; the join stays in the database
A stored procedure — the only object an app is allowed to SELECT from
An AFTER INSERT trigger on Crew that materializes a reporting table
A scalar function that returns the join as nvarchar(max) XML
